tier_contract.adequate_docs: The documentation corpus directly supports the answer.
tier_contract.source_only: Source code supports the answer, but the documentation is absent, incomplete, or contradicts the implemented behavior.
tier_contract.total_gap: Neither the documentation nor indexed SST source provides a supported capability or answer.

questions.use_case: Create and register a reusable component
questions.question: I want to write a new kind of component for my simulation. What are the SST-specific steps I need to follow?
questions.reference_answer: Define a C++ class derived from SST::Component, register it with SST_ELI_REGISTER_COMPONENT, implement the lifecycle behavior it needs, build it as an element library linked with SST Core, and register the resulting library path with sst-register.
questions.notes: Exercises the complete authoring path rather than only class inheritance.

questions.use_case: Create recurring checkpoints under a wall-clock allocation
questions.question: I want SST to checkpoint my simulation every hour. What command-line option should I use?
questions.reference_answer: Run SST with --checkpoint-wall-period=1h followed by the configuration file.
questions.notes: A direct operational lookup with an exact documented example.

questions.use_case: Construct a manually partitioned model across MPI ranks
questions.question: I am writing a configuration for multiple MPI ranks and want to construct only each rank's local portion of the graph. Which parallel-load modes and Python rank APIs should I use?
questions.reference_answer: Use --parallel-load=SINGLE when every rank executes the same configuration script or --parallel-load=MULTI when each rank receives a separate input. In Python, use sst.getMyMPIRank() and sst.getMPIRankCount() to select the local graph portion.
questions.notes: Requires synthesis across command-line and Python API documentation.

questions.use_case: Implement and document an optional component parameter
questions.question: How do I give an SST component parameter a default value, and does the default in SST_ELI_DOCUMENT_PARAMS set it automatically?
questions.reference_answer: Set the runtime default in the component implementation code. The default_value field in SST_ELI_DOCUMENT_PARAMS is informational metadata for users and sst-info; it does not set the runtime default.

terms: defaults must be set in code

questions.notes: Tests a subtle but explicitly documented distinction between ELI metadata and behavior.

questions.use_case: Discover topology or negotiate parameters before simulated time starts
questions.question: My components need to exchange topology information before the run phase. In which lifecycle stage should they do it, and which Link APIs are valid there?
questions.reference_answer: Exchange the information in init(unsigned int phase). Send with Link::sendUntimedData() and poll with Link::recvUntimedData(); event handlers and clock handlers are not active and simulation time remains zero during init.
questions.notes: Represents a common element-development error with lifecycle-sensitive APIs.

questions.use_case: Declare, record, and enable a custom component statistic
questions.question: I declared queue_occupancy with SST_ELI_DOCUMENT_STATISTICS, but SST does not print it. What must the component implementation and Python configuration each do?
questions.reference_answer: SST_ELI_DOCUMENT_STATISTICS declares the statistic's metadata and enable level but does not record values. The component must obtain a typed handle with registerStatistic and add samples with addData. The Python configuration must enable that statistic explicitly, or enable all applicable statistics with a sufficient statistic load level. By default statistics are disabled.

terms: By default, no statistics are generated

questions.notes: Requires understanding both component-side registration and model-side enablement.

questions.use_case: Stripe a physical address range across MemHierarchy memory controllers
questions.question: I have three memHierarchy MemControllers covering 4 GiB and want to stripe addresses across them in 1 MiB chunks. How should I set the address-range and interleave parameters?
questions.reference_answer: Give all three controllers addr_range_end=4294967295. Use addr_range_start values 0, 1048576, and 2097152 respectively, set interleave_size=1MiB on each, and set interleave_step=3MiB on each. Each physical address at a shared hierarchy level must map to only one component.
questions.notes: Adds a concrete SST Elements user workflow so verification is not limited to SST Core APIs.

questions.use_case: Load an additional sstsimulator.conf from a non-default location
questions.question: How can I make SST read an additional SST configuration file from a non-default path without replacing the installed or per-user configuration?
questions.reference_answer: Set SST_CONFIG_FILE_PATH to one or more additional configuration paths. SST reads the install configuration, then the user's ~/.sst/sstsimulator.conf, then paths from SST_CONFIG_FILE_PATH, followed by explicit override paths. Multiple environment paths use SST_CONFIG_FILE_PATH_SEPARATOR, which defaults to ':'.
questions.notes: The documentation describes the configuration file but not these environment variables or their precedence.

questions.use_case: Extract machine-readable run-loop time without setup and teardown
questions.question: I need machine-readable timing for only SST's simulation run loop, excluding model construction and teardown. Which options and JSON path provide it?
questions.reference_answer: Use --timing-info=2 with --profiling-output=FILE.json, then read regions.total.execute.run.duration. The options and JSON output format are documented, but the exact nested path follows SST Core's source-defined performance-region hierarchy.
questions.notes: Tracks SST Core's 2026 performance-reporting redesign; the exact nested JSON path is source-derived and therefore remains a documentation gap.

questions.use_case: Restart a checkpoint with a different rank/thread layout
questions.question: A regular SST 16 checkpoint was created with four MPI ranks and one thread per rank. Can I restart it with two ranks and two threads per rank, and what restrictions apply?
questions.reference_answer: Yes. SST 16 and the current repository can restart a regular checkpoint with new partitioning and parallelism, so 4x1 to 2x2 is supported. Restart repartitioning uses built-in partitioners. A parallel-loaded simulation is the exception: it can restart with the same degree of parallelism but cannot be arbitrarily repartitioned because it lacks a unified configuration graph.

terms: restarted with new partitioning and parallelism

questions.notes: Moved from source_only to adequate_docs after SST 16 documentation added explicit restart-repartitioning behavior and its parallel-load exception.

questions.question: How do I make SST migrate active components between MPI ranks during the run phase to correct load imbalance without restarting?
absence_queries: migrate active components between MPI ranks
questions.notes: A plausible scalability request. SST documents construction-time partitioning and restart repartitioning, not live component migration.

questions.question: How can I record the global SST event schedule from one run and deterministically replay that trace in a later run?
absence_queries: record and replay the event schedule
questions.notes: SST Elements may internally replay blocked memory events; that is distinct from a Core-wide deterministic record/replay facility.

questions.use_case: Fit a simulation model to measured hardware behavior
questions.question: How can SST automatically calibrate my element parameters against measured hardware traces and produce the best-fit parameter set?
questions.notes: A realistic modeling workflow, but not a capability supplied by SST Core or the indexed Elements.
